PUBLIC MARKET DATA

ECB euro-area AAA zero curve

Loading the bundled market snapshot…

The ECB fits this curve to AAA government-bond market data. It is a sovereign benchmark, not an EURIBOR or €STR OIS curve. Select the curve that matches your bond and valuation basis.

The source date is shown for every curve. Browser refresh depends on ECB availability; the bundled snapshot remains available if a refresh fails.

YOUR MARKET DATA

Import a curve workbook

Load provider zero rates or discount factors using the curve template. Give each curve a unique ID and identify EURIBOR projection curves by index.

For convenience, include a “Curves” sheet in your bond workbook. Zero rates use percentage points (3 means 3%) or native Excel percentages; JSON rates use decimals.

ƒ

Market curve inputs must be zero rates or discount factors, not unbootstrapped par swap quotes.
Discount factors are interpolated log-linearly. Coverage, currency, curve date and projection index are checked; curves are never silently extrapolated.

TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN

Follow the flow.

A workflow you trigger. Calculations you can inspect.

The same Python behind every run

The interface reads bond and curve Excel data locally and sends normalized inputs to a Python worker in your browser. The worker calls workflow.py and your bond_engine.py. Results return to the interface for review and Excel export.

The source package includes the application, Python engine, workflow documentation, tests, and GitHub Actions checks. The valuation itself runs when you click “Run valuation”; it does not send your portfolio to GitHub Actions.

NO BLACK BOX

Know what’s behind the number.

Explicit conventions. Inspectable Python. Your workbook stays on your device.

Cash flows & present value

Interest = notional × annual coupon rate × period year fraction. Zero-coupon bonds have one principal payment at maturity and no accrued coupon interest. Principal is repaid once, at maturity. Dirty PV is the sum of discounted future payments; clean PV subtracts accrued interest.

Flat override DF = exp(−r × ACT/365F)

Select a dated discount curve from the market-data library, or use an explicit flat continuously compounded rate. The ECB public curve is an AAA sovereign benchmark; supplied market curves can represent your required credit or funding basis. Dates and sources are recorded in the Excel export.

Floating rate bonds

Choose EURIBOR-1M, EURIBOR-3M, EURIBOR-6M or EURIBOR-12M (or a custom term index with its tenor). The current period requires the known reference fixing, excluding spread. A projection curve must identify that same index; reset frequency must match its tenor. Future rates are simple forwards implied by the projection curve, plus spread.

Forward = (DF(start) / DF(end) − 1) / accrual

EURIBOR fixings and forward curves are not supplied by the ECB sovereign feed: import licensed/provider data or supply a transparent flat projection assumption. Floating forecasts change with rates. Overnight compounded SOFR/SONIA, reset lags, caps, floors, and embedded options are outside this version’s scope.

Dates & conventions

Schedules run backward from maturity, preserve month-end, and allow a short first stub. Supported day counts: ACT/360, ACT/365F and European 30E/360.

There are no business-day or holiday adjustments. Payments on settlement are excluded. This version supports bullet bonds, without amortization, ex-coupon rules, or optionality.

Workbooks & source code

Choose your worksheet and header row, then map columns. Required bond information must be present in the workbook or supplied as a fallback. Arbitrary spreadsheet layouts do not imply missing financial data.

Outputs include Valuations, Cash Flows, Inputs, Curves, Errors, and Run Info, including index names, curve IDs, source dates and age warnings. Currency totals are never combined across currencies.
